arxiv-2107-06040.title: The Cauchy Combination Test under Arbitrary Dependence Structures Thanks: Corresponding author: liqz@amss.ac.cn.
arxiv-2107-06040.creator: Mingya Long
arxiv-2107-06040.description: Abstract Combining individual p p -values to perform an overall test is often encountered in statistical applications. The Cauchy combination test (CCT) ( J Am Stat Assoc , 2020, 115(529): 393-402) is a powerful and computationally efficient approach to integrate individual p p -values under arbitrary dependence structures for sparse signals.

arxiv-2210-13694.title: Worst-Case Adaptive Submodular Cover
arxiv-2210-13694.creator: Jing Yuan, Shaojie Tang
arxiv-2210-13694.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the adaptive submodular cover problem under the worst-case setting. This problem generalizes many previously studied problems, namely, the pool-based active learning and the stochastic submodular set cover. arxiv-2303-15446.title: SwiftFormer: Efficient Additive Attention for Transformer-based Real-time Mobile Vision Applications
arxiv-2303-15446.creator: Abdelrahman Shaker, Muhammad Maaz, Hanoona Rasheed, Salman Khan, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Fahad Shahbaz Khan
arxiv-2303-15446.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Abdelrahman Shaker, Muhammad Maaz, Hanoona Rasheed, Salman Khan, Ming-Hsuan Yang, Fahad Shahbaz Khan. Self-attention has become a defacto choice for capturing global context in various vision applications. However, its quadratic computational complexity with respect to image resolution limits its use in real-time applications, especially for deployment on resource-constrained mobile devices. Although hybrid approaches have been proposed to combine the advantages of convolutions and self-attention for a better speed-accuracy trade-off, the expensive matrix multiplication operations in self-attention remain a bottleneck.

arxiv-2304-01570.title: Revisiting the Red-giant Branch Hosts KOI-3886 and ι \iota Draconis. Detailed Asteroseismic Modeling and Consolidated Stellar Parameters Facilities: Kepler , TESS, Gaia . kepseismic ( https://archive.stsci.edu/prepds/kepseismic/ ), kadacs ( García et al. 2011 ; García et al. 2014 ; Pires et al. 2015
arxiv-2304-01570.creator: Tiago L. Campante, Tanda Li, J. M. Joel Ong, Enrico Corsaro, Margarida S. Cunha, Timothy R. Bedding, Diego Bossini, Sylvain N. Breton, Derek L. Buzasi, William J. Chaplin, Morgan Deal, Rafael A. García, Michelle L. Hill, Marc Hon, Daniel Huber, Chen Jiang, Stephen R. Kane, Cenk Kayhan, James S. Kusz
arxiv-2304-01570.description: Abstract Asteroseismology is playing an increasingly important role in the characterization of red-giant host stars and their planetary systems. Here, we conduct detailed asteroseismic modeling of the evolved red-giant branch (RGB) hosts KOI-3886 and ι \iota Draconis, making use of end-of-mission Kepler (KOI-3886) and multi-sector TESS ( ι \iota Draconis) time-series photometry.

arxiv-2405-17786.title: Effect of insulator end cap thickness on time-dependent Hartmann flow in a rotating mirror
arxiv-2405-17786.creator: Rahul Gaur \aff 1 \corresp, Ian G. Abel \aff 2, Bindesh Tripathi \aff 3, Egemen Kolemen \aff 1,4
arxiv-2405-17786.description: Abstract We present a framework for analyzing plasma flow in a rotating mirror. By making a series of physical assumptions, we reduce the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations in a three-dimensional cylindrical system to a one-dimensional system in a shallow, cuboidal channel within a transverse magnetic field, similar to the Hartmann flow in the ducts.

arxiv-2410-03756.title: The Smart Buildings Control Suite: A Diverse Open Source Benchmark to Evaluate and Scale HVAC Control Policies for Sustainability
arxiv-2410-03756.creator: Judah Goldfeder, Victoria Dean, Zixin Jiang, Xuezheng Wang, Bing Dong, Hod Lipson, John Sipple
arxiv-2410-03756.description: Abstract Commercial buildings account for 17% of U.S. carbon emissions, with roughly half of that from Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC). HVAC devices form a complex thermodynamic system, and while Model Predictive Control and Reinforcement Learning have been used to optimize control policies, scaling to thousands of buildings remains a significant unsolved challenge.

arxiv-2502-02513.title: Diffusion Generative Modeling on Lie Group Representations
arxiv-2502-02513.creator: Marco Bertolini, Tuan Le & Djork-Arné Clevert
arxiv-2502-02513.description: Abstract We introduce a novel class of score-based diffusion processes that operate directly in the representation space of Lie groups. Leveraging the framework of Generalized Score Matching, we derive a class of Langevin dynamics that decomposes as a direct sum of Lie algebra representations, enabling the modeling of any target distribution on any (non-Abelian) Lie group.

arxiv-2602-22750.title: The Inference Bottleneck: Antitrust and Neutrality Duties in the Age of Cognitive Infrastructure
arxiv-2602-22750.creator: Gaston Besanson, Marcelo Celani
arxiv-2602-22750.description: Abstract . As generative AI commercializes, competitive advantage is shifting from one-time model training toward continuous inference, distribution, and routing. At the frontier, large-scale inference can function as cognitive infrastructure: a bottleneck input that downstream applications rely on to compete, controlled by firms that often compete downstream through integrated assistants, productivity suites, and developer tooling.

pmc-10594103.title: Clinical factors and diagnoses associated with inappropriate urine-culture ordering in primary care
pmc-10594103.creator: Marissa Valentine-King, Barbara Trautner, Roger Zoorob, Michael Hansen, Jennifer Matas, Robert Atmar, Larissa Grigoryan
pmc-10594103.description: Background: Inappropriate urine-culture ordering is associated with increased antibiotic prescribing in myriad care environments, including acute and long-term care. In primary care, where urinary tract infections (UTIs) are commonly encountered, the appropriateness of urine-culture ordering has not been well described. We examined the appropriateness of urine-culture ordering and factors associated with inappropriate urine-culture ordering in primary care.

pmc-11496745.title: Precision crop mapping: within plant canopy discrimination of crop and soil using multi-sensor hyperspectral imagery
pmc-11496745.creator: C V S S Manohar Kumar, Sudhanshu Shekhar Jha, Rama Rao Nidamanuri, Vinay Kumar Dadhwal
pmc-11496745.description: Leveraging diverse optomechanical and imaging technologies for precision agriculture applications is gaining attention in emerging economies. The precise spatial detection of plant objects in farms is crucial for optimizing plant-level nutrition and managing pests and diseases. High-resolution remote sensors mounted on drones have been increasingly deployed for large-scale crop mapping and field variability characterization.

pmc-11541823.title: On the trail of CBCT-guided adaptive rectal boost radiotherapy, does daily delineation require a radiation oncologist?
pmc-11541823.creator: Julien Pierrard, David Dechambre, Christel Abdel Massih, Sophie Cvilic, Ana Da Silva Chambel Roma, Pascale Henderickx, Sofie Heylen, Eleonore Longton, Romain Mony, Mohamed Amine Tenabene, Thaïs Tison, Ad Vandermeulen, Loïc Vander Veken, Aniko Wale Etume, Anne-Emmanuella Yeo, Geneviève Van Ooteghem
pmc-11541823.description: Highlights•The rectal boost delineation error is higher in the supero-inferior axis.•The delineation variability is lower among expert ROs.•RTTs don’t need non-expert RO oversight for rectal boost delineation in online-ART.•Individual training could be considered to reduce delineation variability.•AI-generated rectal boost volume is a reliable starting point during online-ART.

pmc-11606207.title: Predicting the time to get back to work using statistical models and machine learning approaches
pmc-11606207.creator: George Bouliotis, M Underwood, R Froud
pmc-11606207.description: BackgroundWhether machine learning approaches are superior to classical statistical models for survival analyses, especially in the case of lack of proportionality, is unknown.ObjectivesTo compare model performance and predictive accuracy of classic regressions and machine learning approaches using data from the Inspiring Families programme.MethodsThe Inspiring Families programme aims to support members of families with complex issues to return to work.

pmc-11638400.title: Does manganese influence grass litter decomposition on a Hawaiian rainfall gradient?
pmc-11638400.creator: Elizabeth L Paulus, Peter M Vitousek
pmc-11638400.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Plant litter is a well-defined pool of organic matter (OM) in which the influence of manganese (Mn) on decomposition (both decomposition rate and the mix of compounds ultimately transferred to soil OM) has been clearly demonstrated in temperate forests. However, no similar study exists on grasslands and the effect of foliar Mn versus soil-derived Mn on litter decomposition is poorly known.

pmc-11772346.title: Mobile-based in-home telerehabilitation compared with in-hospital face-to-face rehabilitation for elderly patients after total hip arthroplasty in China's level 1 trauma center: a noninferiority randomized controlled trial
pmc-11772346.creator: Yang Zhou, Yiming Lyu, Qiaojie Wang, Yanhong Ma, Lihua Huang, Xin Zhang
pmc-11772346.description: BackgroundTelerehabilitation is gaining popularity in European and American countries, but whether it can be successfully implemented in China still lacks support from clinical studies.ObjectiveThis trial aimed to determine if a home-based telerehabilitation method is clinically noninferior to standard in-hospital face-to-face rehabilitation for elderly patients with total hip arthroplasty (THA) in China.

pmc-12494494.title: Recovery of Proteins and Bioactive Peptides From Potato Peels
pmc-12494494.creator: Aytunga Arik Kibar, Özlem Aslan, Halil Dasgin, Emel Önder Fırat, Halil Rıza Avcı, Serhat Koçer, Fatih Tosun
pmc-12494494.description: Potato peels, a significant byproduct of the potato processing industry, hold immense potential for sustainable utilization due to their rich composition of proteins, bioactive peptides, dietary fibers, and phenolic compounds. These components not only present opportunities for functional food development but also align with the principles of a circular economy by reducing waste and creating value‐added products.

pmc-12576817.title: Multivalency Enables Signal Processing at Single Protein Level
pmc-12576817.creator: Xiaoyu Wu, Yuanqi Jia, Tong Zhang, Zhehao Xiong, Zihang Ye, Ge Yu, Yingjie Lei, Zhuo Mao, Vicky Qu, Bobo Dang, Ziyao Xu, Zibo Chen
pmc-12576817.description: Synthetic signal processing in cells can be achieved through complex networks of molecules or simpler, single-molecule-based mechanisms. The latter approach stands out for its reduced genetic load and ease of delivery. Multivalent protein binders are such single-molecule signal processors that exhibit distinct behaviors when interacting with cells presenting various antigen profiles.

pmc-12820057.title: Reduced graphene oxide promoted by SnO2 for photodegradation of tetracycline in water
pmc-12820057.creator: Asrin Bahrami, Donya Mohammadi, Faranak Akhlaghian
pmc-12820057.description: Reduced graphene oxide, with a high specific surface area and conductivity, also exhibits photocatalytic activity, and its photocatalytic performance improves with the addition of semiconductors. In this study, SnO2/reduced graphene oxide (RGO) composite was applied for tetracycline removal from water under visible light irradiation. The photocatalytic performance of RGO was enhanced through SnO2 deposition.

pmc-12837022.title: The melorheostosis with severe knee and ankle deformity treated by total knee arthroplasty with V-Y quadricepsplasty: a case report and literature review
pmc-12837022.creator: Zhao-Yu Chen, Hao-Tian Wu, Dan Xing, Qiang Liu, Yan Ke, Jian-Hao Lin
pmc-12837022.description: BackgroundMelorheostosis is a rare disease with a classical radiological performance appearing as the sign of skeletal hyperostosis like dripping wax flowing down from candle. The pathological bone hyperostosis and soft tissue fibrosis frequently resulted in intolerable pain and functional loss. Due to the low incidence of 0.9 per million, the management for the disease is rarely reported.

pmc-13136197.title: WOMAC-based recovery after total knee arthroplasty in a multiethnic Asian cohort: a 5-year registry-based study of interval-specific predictors of improvement
pmc-13136197.creator: Eau Liang Teow, Xin Zhang, Wei Loong Barry Tan, Chee Hoe Kong, Harish Sivasubramanian, Xun Li, Melvin Kian Loong Tan, Zi Qiang Glen Liau, Nick Bansback, Nan Luo, Wai San Wilson Tam, Ling Jie Cheng
pmc-13136197.description: BackgroundPatient-reported outcomes (PROs) after total knee arthroplasty (TKA) are well-documented in Western populations, but long-term recovery and its determinants in multiethnic Asian populations remain poorly understood. We aimed to characterise 5-year WOMAC recovery after TKA and to identify patient, clinical, and surgical factors associated with the odds of improvement at each consecutive postoperative interval in a multiethnic Asian cohort.

pmc-13230846.title: Higher job exposures are associated with reduced return-to-work two years after rehabilitation in a nationwide cohort study based on German Pension Insurance data
pmc-13230846.creator: Martin Brünger, Paul Gellert
pmc-13230846.description: Return-to-work (RTW) after medical rehabilitation is an important indicator of post-rehabilitation labour market participation, yet evidence on its association with occupation-based job exposure over longer follow-up periods remains limited. This nationwide retrospective cohort study examined the association between job exposure and RTW within 24 months post-rehabilitation using routine administrative data from the German Pension Insurance.

pmc-13280225.title: Assessment of humoral immune responses elicited by an inactivated lumpy skin disease vaccine in cattle: a preliminary study
pmc-13280225.creator: Amarin RITTIPORNLERTRAK, Tawatchai SINGHLA, Pongpisid KOONYOSYING, Anucha MUENTHAISONG, Kanokwan SANGKAKAM, Thanya VARINRAK, Nisachon APINDA, Boondarika NAMBOOPPHA, Khwanchai KREAUSUKON, Nattawooti STHITMATEE
pmc-13280225.description: The control of lumpy skin disease (LSD) is often hampered by adverse effects associated with currently available live attenuated vaccines (LAVs). This preliminary study was therefore designed to determine the immune responses in dairy cattle immunized with either an inactivated LSD vaccine (derived from a local strain) or a commercial LAV.

pmc-13524477.title: Broiler performance, intestinal adaptation, and environmental responses to graded dietary inclusion of bacterial single-cell protein
pmc-13524477.creator: Mahfuza Ferdous, M Elizabeth E Ball, James C Wangui, Ramesh Selvaraj, Ilias Kyriazakis
pmc-13524477.description: We evaluated the effects of replacing soybean meal (SBM) with Methylococcus capsulatus bacterial single-cell protein (BSCP) at varying inclusion levels and early dietary exposure on broiler performance, gut physiology, nutrient utilization, and environmental emissions. A total of 480-day-old Ross 308 broilers were allocated to six dietary treatments across starter (d0–10), grower (d11–21), and finisher (d22–35) phases.
